thread:
emma_support: Customer reports 403 when trying to edit project settings in the console. They see their role as 'Project Admin' in the members list but buttons are greyed out.

raj_engineer: thanks — can you paste the user id + org id? also, do they authenticate via Okta or Google?

emma_support: user: u-8692, org: org-741, auth: Okta SSO via OIDC. Repro steps attached from customer: log in -> open org -> switch to project -> see 'Project Admin' badge -> try to change billing contact -> 403.

maria_sre: quick check — can they perform any API calls with their token? ask them to try curl to rule out UI bug.

emma_support: customer ran: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...user-token..." \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-741" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects/proj-12/settings
```
response: 403 {"error":"permission_denied","reason":"action_not_allowed"}  — they attached JWT claims screenshot.

raj_engineer: paste the claims snippet? need to check roles/scopes in token (scope vs role mapping can diverge).

emma_support: claims: 
```
{"sub":"u-8692","email":"j.smith@cust.com","roles":["project_admin"],"groups":["prod-team"],"org":"org-741","project_ids":["proj-12"]}
```

maria_sre: interesting — token lists project_ids but our authn layer expects org-scoped roles mapped via SCIM groups, not project_ids in the token. Could be a token claim name mismatch from the IdP.

ops-bot: idp-sync: last SCIM sync for org-741 completed 2026-09-30T22:12:03Z, changes queued: 2.

raj_engineer: ok hypothesis: Okta recently changed the claim name from "project_ids" to "projects" in the outgoing assertion and customer has mixed sessions. That would make the UI show roles from SCIM cache but the API enforcement uses the token claims during operations -> 403.

emma_support: customer says they rotated apps yesterday, could match. They can reproduce by creating a new Okta session (incognito) and still see 403.

maria_sre: ask them to POST a call to /auth/debug with the token so we can log exact claim keys server-side. If that's sensitive, have them paste the decoded JWT header+payload (redact jti).

emma_support: customer pasted payload: claim key is "projects" (array) not "project_ids". so mismatch confirmed.

raj_engineer: short-term workaround: (1) have admin invite the user to the project directly via console (member invite) — that bypasses claim-based auto-bind. (2) Or they can use a personal API key tied to the project. We'll advise both.

support_escalations: tagging eng-infra for a persistent fix — we need to accept both claim keys during a 30d transition window and add a warning in console when claim names don't match SCIM. @eng-infra please triage?

maria_sre: action items:
- Emma: provide the customer's Okta app id + recent SCIM logs (we have ops-bot showing queued changes).
- Raj: implement claim alias acceptance in authz middleware (quick patch).
- Ops-bot: schedule a forced SCIM resync for org-741 and invalidate sessions for stale tokens.

ops-bot: scim-resync triggered for org-741 by support request. ETA ~5m.

emma_support: customer confirmed after resync + admin invite they can edit settings now. They accepted temporary invite as workaround.

raj_engineer: will open a patch PR to treat "projects" and "project_ids" equivalently in token parsing. Mark as hotfix with rollback.

maria_sre: note for runbook: if UI shows role but API blocks -> suspect claim-name drift between IdP and our token parser, check SCIM sync + decoded JWT.

support_escalations: marking resolved for now. escalate to SSO product lead to consider adding telemetry that flags claim-name mismatches in the future. :thumbsup:

emma_support: thanks everyone — closing with customer happy and workaround documented.
